title: The Verified Remit-To Change
scenario_text: Jasper Freight's accounts payable team receives an emailed request to update banking details for an established vendor, "Coastal Diesel Supply," ahead of paying invoice INV-77120 for $258,000 (fuel and lubricants delivered and confirmed received). The email arrives from ap@coastaldieselsupply.com, the domain of record, and asks that payment go to a new account: routing 121000358 / account ending 4602. Jasper's vendor master shows the prior remit-to as routing 121000358 / account ending 1195 at the same bank. Per Jasper's banking-change control, AP initiates an out-of-band callback to the vendor's controller using the phone number stored in the vendor master (not any number from the email). Jasper's control also requires that the account-holder name on any supporting bank letter be matched against the vendor's W-9 legal name before any funds are released. The controller answers, confirms she personally submitted the change, and states the company recently opened account ending 4602 at the same institution and is closing the old account ending 1195. The updated banking matches a voided check and a bank-verification letter the controller emails on the master-file domain, and the account holder name on the letter is "Coastal Diesel Supply, Inc.," matching the vendor's W-9. The invoice itself is undisputed and approved for payment. AP must decide how much to release to the newly requested account ending 4602.
question: How much should Jasper Freight release to the account ending 4602 specified in the change request?
